# The Mechanism of `CORRECTION + CONJUNCTION` 

## Component Definition

### `CORRECTION` 
By adopting the definition by Lascarides & Asher (2009), `CORRECTION` is considered as divergent (non-veridical) subordinating rhetorical relation embedding a denial, as quoted here:

> Asher and Lascarides (2003, p363) stipulates that in the absence of divergent rhetorical relations (in other words, speech acts of denial such as *Correction* and *Counterevidence*), all the content is agreed upon. So SDRT wrongly predicts that (1c) is agreed upon.

and:

>Let 〈Π, F, last〉 be an SDRS. Furthermore, where π1, π2 ∈ Π, we say that π1 > π2 iff either: (i) R(π1, π2) is within the range of F , where R is a subordinating relation (e.g., Q-Elab, Plan-Elab, IQAP, Correction, Background, Elaboration, Explanation); or ... 

According to the same paper, the semantics of Correction is defined as 

$$(w, f) \llbracket \mathit{Correction}(\pi_1, \pi_2) \rrbracket_m (w', g) \text{ iff } (w, f) \llbracket (\neg K_{\pi_1}) \land K_{\pi_2} \land \varphi_{\mathit{Correction}(\pi_1, \pi_2)} \rrbracket_m (w', g)$$

## Fundamental Rules of SBN 
* Accessibility: (a) neither positive nor negative indices can enter negated context, and (b) only negative indices in negated contexts can refer to discourse referents outside the negation. 

## Rules of Annotating Self-Repair
* Always use `CORRECTION` to quarantine the reparandum, and use `CONJUNCTION` to merge the content afterwards back to the upper context. 
* Always follow the Fundamental Rules of SBN
* Always ignore interregna in the transcription, but retain them in the annotation on the right hand side of `%`. Common English interregna include but are not limited to "I mean", "well", "actually", "no", and "in fact". 

# Covered Cases 
**For demonstration purpose, all the synstets in the examples are written as `.01`, with a few exceptions, which does not represent the actual synset in WordNet.**
## One-Sentence Cases

### SV Sentence
"The boy sneezed, I mean, coughed"

```sbn
boy.n.01.                      % The boy
time.n.08 TPR now              
    CORRECTION <1
sneeze.v.01 Agent -1 Time -1.  % sneezed, I mean,
    CONJUNCTION <2
cough.v.01 Agent -3 Time -2    % coughed
```

### SVO Sentence

#### Subject Self-repair 
"Josh, no, Mary plays tennis well"

```sbn
entity.n.01                          
    CORRECTION <1
male.n.02 Name "Josh" EQU -1         % Josh, no,
    CONJUNCTION <2                   
female.n.02 Name "Mary" EQU -2       % Mary
play.v.01 Agent -3 Time +1 Theme +2  % plays
time.n.08 EQU now                    
tennis.n.01                          % tennis !!!well程度副词在SBN里显示吗？这个先挂着，写完了回头一起处理
```

#### Verb Self-repair
"The cat chases, actually, hunts the rat"
This case of representation has not been fully decided yet. Depends on allowing the nodes in the `CORRECTION` box being free loading or not, we have two temporal notations:

```sbn
cat.n.01
rat.n.01
time.n.08 EUQ now
    CORRECTION <1 Agent -3 Theme -2  
chase
    CONJUNCTION <2
hunt
```
If SBN allows not fulfilling every semantic roles for a predicate, the following one should also be legal, meanwhile, following the natural language order.

```sbn
cat.n.01
time.n.08 EUQ now
    CORRECTION <1
chase Agent -2 Time -1
    CONJUNCTION <2
hunt Agent -3 Theme +1 Time -2 
rat.n.01
```

#### Object Self-repair
"I ordered a banana bread, I mean, a cherry pie"

```sbn
person.n.01 EQU speaker              % I
time.n.01 TPR now                    % ordered
order.v.01 Agent -2 Time -1          %
    CORRECTION <1                    %
banana_bread.n.01 ThemeOf -1         % a banana bread, I mean
    CONJUNCTION <2                   %
cherry_pie.n.01 ThemeOf -2           % a cherry pie
```

### Negation
"I didn't order a banana bread, I mean, a cherry pie"

```sbn
person.n.01 EQU speaker              % I
time.n.01 TPR now                    % 
NEGATION <1                          % didn't
order.v.01 Agent -2 Time -1          % order
  CORRECTION <1                      %
banana_bread.n.01 ThemeOf-1          % a banana bread,
  CONJUNCTION <2                     %
cherry_pie.n.01 ThemeOf -2           % a cherry pie
```

### Adjunct 
"The class is on Monday, no, on Tuesday"

```sbn
class.n.01                               % The class
time.n.08 EQU now                        %
be.v.01 Theme -2 Time -1                 % is on
  CORRECTION <1                          % 
time.n.08 Day "Monday" TimeOf -1         % Monday,
  CONJUNCTION <2                         % no, on 
time.n.08 Day "Tuesday" TimeOf -2        % Tuesday.
```

### Preposition replacement
"I went to, I mean, from the school"

```sbn
person.n.01 EQU speaker                    % I
run.v.01 Theme -1 Time +1                  % ran
time.n.08 TPR now                          %
CORRECTION <1                              %
event.v.01 EQU -2 Destination +1           % to
entity.n.01                                %
CONJUNCTION <2                             %
event.v.01 EQU -4 Source +1                % I mean from
school.n.02                                % the school.
```

### Universal Quantification - Donkey sentence
"If a farmer owns a donkey, he beats, I mean, feeds it."
Notice the difference with the SBN of verb self-repair. In the current case, the reparandum verb *beat* locates in the consequence (right) clause. It means the reparandum needs to travel across two boxex (`NEGATION` and `CORRECTION`) to reach all the nodes. 

```sbn
NEGATION <1                              % Every/If
farmer.n.01                              % farmer
own.v.01 Pivot -1 Theme +1               % who owns a
donkey.n.01                              % donkey,
NEGATION <2                              % he
entity.n.01 EQU -1                       % it
    CORRECTION <1                        %
beat.v.01 Agent -4 Patient -1            % beats (reparandum)
    CONJUNCTION <2                       %
feed.v.01 Agent -5 Patient -2            % feeds it
```

Compared to an ordinary donkey sentence without self-repair, extracted from Bos (2021):
"Every farmer who owns a donkey beats it" 

```sbn
    NEGATION -1                 % Every 
farmer.n.01                     % farmer
own.v.01 Pivot -1  Theme +1     % who owns
donkey.n.01  NEGATION -1        % a donkey
beat.v.01 Agent -3  Patient +1  % beats
entity.n.01 EQU -2              % it
```
It is notetaking that in the "ordinary" donkey sentence, the pronoun "it" follows the natural language oder by appearing by the end of the SBN sequence. However, in the sel-repair variety, it is moved forward to satisfy the two rules above. 

### Retracting and Forwarding Repairs

#### Retracting Repair 
"Bill said you will put, I mean, you will drop the ball on the table" (Husband, 2015)

```sbn
male.n.02 Name "Bill"                              % Bill           
say.v.01                                           % said
Proposition >1                                     %
Agent -1                                           %
Time +1                                            %
time.n.08 TPR now                                  %
CONTINUATION <0                                    %
person.n.01 EQU hearer                             % you
time.n.08 TSU now                                  % will
    CORRECTION <1                                  %
put.v.01 Agent -2 Time -1 Theme +2 Destination +3  % put [Positive Index Alert!!]
    CONJUNCTION <2                                 % I mean,               
drop.v.01 Agent -3 Time -2 Theme +1 Destination +2 % drop 
ball.n.01                                          % the ball
table.n.02                                         % on the table 
```

#### Forwarding Self-Repair
"Josh drove, no, Marsha drove the old car to the church"

```sbn
entity.n.01
    CORRECTION <1
male.n.02 Name "Josh" EQU -1             % Josh
drive.v.03 Agent -1 Time +1 Theme +3     % drove
time.n.08 TPR now 
    CONJUNCTION <2                       % no
female.n.02 Name "Marsha" EQU -4         % Marsha
drive.v.03 Agent -1 Time +1 Theme +2     % drove [Positive index aleart!!]
time.n.08 TPR now                        %
old.a.02 Value +1                        % the old 
car.n.01 Attribute -1 Destination +1     % car
church.n.02                              % to the church
```

## Multiple-Sentence (Discourse) Cases
### Anaphora referring to both reparandum and repair 
"A: My favourite dessert is banana bread, actually, cherry pie. B: They are both good desserts"

```sbn
% Utterance 1
person.n.01 EQU speaker                    % node 1
favourite.a.02 Experiencer -1 Stimulus +1  % node 2
dessert.n.01                               % node 3
be.v.02 Theme -1 Time +1 Co-Theme +2       % node 4
time.n.08 EQU now                          % node 5
    CORRECTION <1
banana_bread.n.01                          % node 6  (reparandum)
CONJUNCTION <2
cherry_pie.n.01 Co-ThemeOf -3              % node 7  (repair)

% Utterance 2
CONTINUATION <1
entity.n.01 ANA -2 ANA -1                  % node 8: refers to nodes 6 and 7
time.n.08 EQU now                          % node 9
good.a.01 AttributeOf -2 Time -1           % node 10
dessert.n.01                               % node 11
```

###  Intra-utterance Self-Repair Combined with Cross-turn
"A: Joe bought a Ferrari, I mean, a Jaguar, as a birthday gift. B: No, he bought it as a wedding gift."

```sbn
% A's utterance — Context 0
person.n.01 Name "Joe"                    % Joe
time.n.01 TPR now                         %
buy.v.01 Agent -2 Time -1 Manner +3       % bought
    CORRECTION <1                         % I mean, [sub-clausal]
car.n.01 Name "Ferrari" ThemeOf -1        % a Ferrari — Context 1 (reparandum)
    CONJUNCTION <2                        %
car.n.01 Name "Jaguar" ThemeOf -2         % a Jaguar — merged into Context 0
gift.n.01 PartOf "birthday"               % as a birthday gift
% Discourse boundary
CORRECTION <1                             % No, [discourse-level] — Context 2
% B's utterance
male.n.01 EQU -6                          % he
buy.v.01 Agent -1 Theme -3 Manner +1      % bought it
gift.n.01 PartOf "wedding"                % as a wedding gift
```
